title: An owner for any kind of handle
description:
Windows has many handle types, each closed by a different function. Write `ScopedResource`, an RAII owner that works for all of them: it holds a raw value of type `void*` and a pointer to the function that closes it.

- The constructor takes the value and the close function. The value `nullptr` and the value `kInvalid` (which stands in for `INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE`) both mean "nothing owned".
- The destructor calls the close function on the value, if something is owned.
- `release()` gives up ownership without closing, returning the value.
- `reset()` closes whatever is owned now and becomes empty.
- `get()` returns the value; `owns()` says whether something is owned.
- It can be **moved** (ownership passes to the new object, the old one becomes empty) but not copied.

The tests use a pretend close function that counts calls, so this runs anywhere.
hints: `owns()` is true when the value is neither `nullptr` nor `kInvalid`. `reset()` calls the close function only when `owns()` is true, then sets the value to `nullptr`. The destructor just calls `reset()`.
`std::exchange(x, nullptr)` returns the old value of `x` and sets it to `nullptr` in one step: exactly what `release` and the moves need.
Move assignment must close what the target already owns before taking the other object's value: `reset();` first.
